stories.h: Fincher's Cliff Booth spin-off is a knockout
stories.why: Fincher plus Tarantino, the big prestige release
sum: David Fincher directs Quentin Tarantino's script for this spin-off of Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, with Brad Pitt back as stuntman Cliff Booth. It's 1977, and a job for agent Karen Crosby's client (Elizabeth Debicki plays Karen) pulls Cliff into a dangerous deal, while a light romance with Karen runs alongside the crime plot.

Little White Lies calls it a wildly entertaining crime fantasia. The review credits Fincher with reining in Tarantino's usual excess and steering the story toward real relationships, and compares it to Jackie Brown. Cliff's charm still hides darker traits, and the film only almost manages to square them. It runs 143 minutes and is out 25 November.
pts: Brad Pitt, Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan
Rated 4/5/5 (anticipation, enjoyment, in retrospect)
Out 25 Nov, 143 min
stories.q: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth

stories.h: You Can See Everything: Fielder's Holmes doc dazzles
stories.why: Smart, genre-bending documentary event
sum: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's A24 documentary follows Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes and her husband Billy Evans in the weeks before she goes to federal prison. Amanda Seyfried and Christopher Abbott also appear. The film cares less about whether Holmes is guilty than about how truth gets shaped, staged and exploited.

Little White Lies calls it an engrossing look at truth itself and says the line between fiction and non-fiction is arbitrary. The reviewer adds that a second viewing shows how the film is built, and singles out Seyfried as a grounding presence. It runs three hours and has already made about $90m in North America.
pts: Rated 4/5/5 by LWLies
180 minutes; in cinemas from 20 Nov
About $90m in North America already

stories.h: Hunger Games prequel is a thrilling return to form
stories.why: The weekend's big blockbuster, well reviewed
sum: Francis Lawrence's Sunrise on the Reaping goes back 24 years before Katniss, to a 16-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) in District 12, who is forced into the 50th Hunger Games, a Quarter Quell. The supporting cast includes Mckenna Grace, Jesse Plemons, Elle Fanning and Ralph Fiennes.

Little White Lies calls it a gripping, emotionally bruising prequel that brings back the feel of the original films after the muted Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes. Zada is singled out as a standout, balancing charm and vulnerability, and the arena design is praised. It opened 20 November and runs 158 minutes.
pts: Joseph Zada stars as young Haymitch
Rated 5/4/4 by LWLies
In cinemas now, 158 min
stories.q: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping

stories.h: Filipiñana: a mesmerising Southeast Asian class satire
stories.why: A regional gem close to home
sum: Rafael Manuel's debut feature is set at a Manila golf resort, seen through Isabel, a 17-year-old tee girl from the Ilocos. Her story runs alongside that of Clara, a Filipino expat from New York who is connected to the resort's owner, over one long summer day. It won a Sundance special jury award and is the Philippines' Oscar entry.

Little White Lies calls it a sumptuous debut whose candy-coloured, Wes Anderson-like look hides real cruelty. The workers are kept at the edges of the frame, and the rich ignore them by choice. The review grants the Parasite comparison but finds the film distinctly Filipino, and says its restrained violence is all the more unsettling.
pts: Philippines' Oscar submission
Rated 4/4/4 by LWLies
UK release 20 Nov, 101 min

stories.h: Golshifteh Farahani magnetic in Kabul thriller
stories.why: Festival discovery with a star turn
sum: When She Hears The Bells, Chabname Zariab's debut feature, premiered in Tallinn Black Nights' First Feature competition. In Kabul in 2021, recently widowed Leila (Golshifteh Farahani) takes a cooking job at a house where trafficked boys are forced to dance for men. Appalled, she decides to act as the Taliban close in on the city.

Screen's Wendy Ide praises the taut, atmospheric storytelling, the propulsive pace and Farahani's commanding presence. Casablanca makes a convincing Kabul, and curtains and burkas are used as symbols of women's vulnerability. Her reservations: the restaurant owner who drives the climax is thinly drawn, and the brisk third act ends abruptly.
pts: 83-minute France/Germany/Belgium debut
Next stop: the Torino festival
Lean, urgent; ending feels rushed

stories.h: Memories Of Lightning flips true crime on its head
stories.why: An experimental pick for arthouse fans
sum: Riccardo Giacconi's 73-minute France/Italy film won IDFA's experimental Envision award after premiering at Venice. It poses as a making-of documentary about a radio journalist investigating the 1982 murder of a 14-year-old girl in a village in Le Marche, a killing local silence has buried. But the journalist is played by an actress, and sound and image often don't match.

Screen's Lee Marshall calls it a dense, cerebral experiment, a kind of ghost story haunting the film's own fabric. It sits between arthouse cinema and art installation. Whether it works depends on whether you enjoy the misdirection more than you resent it. The IDFA win may bring it more festival dates.
pts: IDFA Envision winner, premiered at Venice
Fake documentary playing with true crime
For adventurous viewers

stories.h: Hunger Games and Holmes doc go wide in UK
stories.why: What's drawing crowds this weekend
sum: This weekend Lionsgate opens The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping in 660 UK and Ireland cinemas, the franchise's widest launch, after nearly £2m from Wednesday previews. A24's Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything opens in about 590 venues, the widest release ever for a non-music documentary there.

Also opening: Helen Mirren in Anton Corbijn's Patricia Highsmith drama A Talent For Murder (353 sites), Mahershala Ali in Bassam Tariq's Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother (215), and Sundance titles Josephine and Filipiñana. Last week's leader was Johnny Depp's Ebenezer, which opened at $42m worldwide.
pts: Hunger Games: nearly £2m in previews
Widest non-music doc release ever
Ebenezer led last weekend

stories.h: Scorsese, Binoche join outcry over Panahi sentence
stories.why: World cinema's biggest freedom story
sum: Martin Scorsese, Juliette Binoche, Agnieszka Holland, Walter Salles and Julie Delpy have signed an appeal against the prison sentence handed to Iranian director Jafar Panahi. The appeal is led by the International Coalition for Filmmakers at Risk and is nearing 1,400 signatures, including the heads of the major festivals and the European Film Academy.

Tehran's Revolutionary Court sentenced the Palme d'Or winner (It Was Just An Accident) in absentia to five years and one month in prison. The ruling also seizes his assets, freezes his bank accounts and bans him from travel and social media for two years. The exact charges are unclear and the ruling can be appealed.
pts: Five-year sentence given in absentia
Appeal nears 1,400 signatures
Cannes issued its own condemnation

stories.h: Doha Film Festival opens despite the war
stories.why: Asian and Middle Eastern festival scene
sum: The Doha Film Festival opened despite the ongoing Iran-US war. Festival director Fatma Hassan Alremaihi said organisers could have cancelled but chose not to. The opening film was Sara Ishaq's The Station, set in a women-only petrol station in Yemen that becomes a refuge during the civil war.

The Doha Film Institute backed over 100 projects from 56 countries this year. Its Qumra incubator moved online, and Doha's airport opened its first cinema. Nandita Das and Taim Hassan received honorary awards. The festival runs to 27 November, with over $300,000 in prizes across four competitions.
pts: Opening film: Sara Ishaq's The Station
Runs until 27 November
Over $300,000 in prizes

stories.h: Bill Hader's horror debut They Know finds US home
stories.why: Barry creator moves into horror
sum: Black Bear has bought North American rights to They Know, the first feature Bill Hader has directed, after a competitive bidding process. Hader stars with Linda Cardellini in the psychological horror, about a man who suspects his ex-wife's new partner is having a sinister influence on their children.

The story comes from an idea by Hader and his Barry collaborator Duffy Boudreau. MRC is fully financing the film, which is in post-production, and FilmNation showed footage to buyers in Toronto. No release date has been set.
pts: Hader's first feature as director
Co-stars Linda Cardellini
No release date yet

stories.h: Atlas Sound returns with surprise album Thanatos
stories.why: Deerhunter-era indie rock royalty is back
sum: Bradford Cox has dropped Thanatos without warning, his first full-length as Atlas Sound since 2011's Parallax and his first album of any kind since Deerhunter's 2019 record. The 10 songs, most already road-tested at Philadelphia's Making Time festival in September, were recorded alone in his Atlanta attic on a portable Tascam 8-track and come out on 4AD.

Cox frames it as the final part of a trilogy with Logos and Parallax. It's digital-only for now, with vinyl due next year, and arrives with a scent map pairing a smell to each track plus a bio by Cate Le Bon. Live dates so far: Big Ears, Kilby Block Party and Primavera Sound in spring 2027.
pts: First Atlas Sound album in 15 years, out now on 4AD
Recorded solo on a home 8-track; closes the Logos/Parallax trilogy
Vinyl next year; Primavera Sound date in June

stories.h: Stereogum's 5 best songs: Julien Baker tops the week
stories.why: Five fresh indie and alt picks in one go
sum: Stereogum's weekly countdown is led by Julien Baker's "Hound," a sparse piano-and-acoustic song about chasing dopamine that the writers say lands like breaking out of a cage. Ryley Walker's "Cloud Of Beaujolais" takes second, nodding to his folk roots while drifting somewhere noisier and stranger.

Also on the list: Erika de Casier's hazy, late-arriving lullaby "Whispers"; Philip Frobos's propulsive post-punk track "Fulton County Stadium At 8:05AM," with Mastodon's Bill Kelliher, which uses a 1997 stadium implosion to mourn lost manners; and Awning's half-asleep "I'm Up," which jolts awake with a sudden guitar burst.
pts: No. 1: Julien Baker, "Hound"
Ryley Walker, Erika de Casier, Philip Frobos and Awning round it out
A quick indie playlist for the weekend

stories.h: Radie Peat's solo debut finds tenderness in old tragedies
stories.why: Haunting folk for fans of Lankum and Beth Gibbons
sum: Lankum and ØXN singer Radie Peat's first solo album, No Human Tongue Can Tell, collects traditional songs she felt were too personal for her band. Playing around ten instruments herself, with producer John "Spud" Murphy, she wraps murder ballads and tales of abandoned women in soft, almost Enya-like textures. The review argues that beauty makes the stories harder to shrug off.

Highlights include a gorgeous "Down in the Willow Garden" and a reworked "The Moon and Stars," which gives the narrator's anger more weight and leaves it unresolved. The reviewer hears Shirley Collins and Anne Briggs in the DNA and calls it an unflinching debut, with the gentler moments as its real surprise.
pts: Debut solo LP from Lankum's Radie Peat, out 13 Nov
Dark folk with soothing textures; nearly all played by Peat
Scored 8/10
stories.q: Radie Peat No Human Tongue Can Tell

stories.h: beabadoobee announces second album in months, Bananas 4 Cats
stories.why: Indie-rock favourite with Asia dates ahead
sum: Hot on the heels of 2026's Pylon, beabadoobee has announced Bananas 4 Cats, out 19 February on Dirty Hit/Interscope. Lead single "No Punctuation" is a song fans have been waiting on since snippets leaked more than four years ago.

She calls the new record the opposite side of Pylon: written and recorded at home in East London with a friend, her partner and her cats, it is smaller and more intimate. Pylon went top 10 in the US and gave her a second straight UK No. 1. Her Powerlines tour reaches Australia, New Zealand and Asia in March and April 2027.
pts: Bananas 4 Cats due 19 Feb; single "No Punctuation" out now
A homemade, intimate companion to Pylon
Asia tour leg in March to April 2027

stories.h: Phoebe Bridgers covers Adrianne Lenker's "Anything" for charity
stories.why: Two indie heavyweights on one song
sum: Phoebe Bridgers has released her take on Big Thief singer Adrianne Lenker's "Anything," sampling Lenker's original. Both artists are giving their proceeds to the Palestine Children's Relief Fund. Bridgers co-produced it with Tony Berg, Ethan Gruska and Jack Antonoff, who covers bells, harpsichord, synths and vocoder, with Blake Mills on acoustic guitar.

It continues her tradition of holiday charity covers after songs by Tom Waits, Merle Haggard and The Handsome Family. It's her first since 2022, and it lands mid-way through the Lost Tour for her album Lost Weekend, which returns to North America in February and plays both Coachella weekends.
pts: Cover of Adrianne Lenker's "Anything"; proceeds to PCRF
Produced with Antonoff, Gruska and Tony Berg
Her first holiday charity cover since 2022
stories.q: Phoebe Bridgers Anything Adrianne Lenker cover

stories.h: Bintaro alt-rockers The Sabili drop two singles ahead of debut LP
stories.why: Local alt-rock from greater Jakarta
sum: The Sabili, an alternative rock four-piece from Bintaro, released "Annihilation" and "Ooze" on 13 November as the first look at their debut album, Wave of the Overture. It has eight tracks and is due in early 2027. The band describes the album as an emotional arc from sadness to anger, with deliberately vague lyrics about social issues, tragedy and the grind of city life.

Guitarist Abdul layers harmonics over distortion with shimmer and room-reverb textures, while bassist Gitari had room to improvise fills. The band hopes to play Los Frequencies in the Central Java highlands and share stages with their Pokta Collective peers.
pts: Singles "Annihilation" and "Ooze" out now
Debut LP Wave of the Overture due early 2027
Shoegazey guitar textures, lyrics about social issues

stories.h: Avhath finally release a debut album, 14 years in
stories.why: Heavy end of Indonesia's indie scene
sum: Long known as Indonesia's band without an album, Avhath have released a self-titled debut. Pophariini's reviewer sees it as the work of a matured group. Guitarist Rey produced it, and it fuses black metal, hardcore and death metal with fresher arrangements, heavier palm-muted riffs and drumming that moves from steady beats into blast beats. The reviewer hears touches of Chat Pile and Blood Incantation.

Standouts include the playful riff in "amassed," the bass-led "Recurrence" and the bleak, spoken-word closer "Cinereal Gaze." The catch: the fragmented songs took more than ten listens to stick, and the album is slightly less experimental than the Ephemeral Passage EP. Still, the review calls it close to a masterpiece.
pts: Self-titled debut after 14 years together
Blackened hardcore with death-metal heft; produced by guitarist Rey
Rewards repeat listens; no numeric score

stories.h: Nothing new from Beyoncé or Kendrick Lamar today
stories.why: Checked every morning
sum: No releases, tour dates, features or announcements in the last 24 hours.

stories.h: Telfar drops varsity and moto pieces, plus a big sale
stories.why: Telfar news, sporty unisex layers
sum: Telfar's site added a new batch of outerwear on 18 November: Delancey varsity jackets in blue or black ($580), a heather-grey Delancey hooded bomber ($440), brown or washed-black fleece moto jackets ($530) with matching moto sweatpants ($515), a black crocodile zip sweater ($495) and a blue Varsity Skully beanie ($78).

The Danke plastic bag, in Regular ($148) and Jumbo ($195) black, landed a week earlier. A sale is also running: shopping and circle bags up to 50% off, apparel up to 70% off, and a free $50 Baby Bag charm on orders over $250.
pts: New outerwear went live 18 Nov: varsity jackets, bomber, moto fleece
Danke plastic bag in Regular and Jumbo sizes
Sale: bags up to 50% off, apparel up to 70% off

stories.h: Chopova Lowena x Dr. Martens: punk boots with charms
stories.why: Rock-meets-whimsy, niche label
sum: London label Chopova Lowena and Dr. Martens have released their first collab, a three-piece take on the Aurix sole in red tartan, indigo faux fur and leather with yellow welt stitching. The Aurix Hi LLT is a knee-high boot hung with butterfly charms. The Aurix 5i is a square-toe five-eye lace-up with leaf charms on every eyelet, and the Aurix MJ is a chunky Mary Jane with a butterfly buckle.
Amy Taylor of Amyl and the Sniffers fronts the campaign. The boots went on sale 19 November on both brands' sites and at selected stores.
pts: Three Aurix styles in red tartan and faux fur
Butterfly and leaf charms, yellow stitching
Out 19 Nov; Amyl and the Sniffers' Amy Taylor fronts it

stories.h: UP THERE x New Balance 1890 gets a rainbow lace cover
stories.why: Colorful, playful runner from a niche store
sum: Melbourne store UP THERE has redone the New Balance 1890 for its "Horizon" release, swapping mesh for shiny nylon and natural suede with debossed details. The base is Castlerock Grey, a heritage NB shade, with Cerulean Blue and Scarlet Red pops inspired by Australian skies.

The standout is a removable lace cover in an iridescent rainbow finish. Three lace options come in the box, so you can tone it down. UP THERE's signature green insole is back. It drops 27 November for AUD 280 (about USD 185), sold through UP THERE.
pts: Grey, blue and red nylon and suede
Removable rainbow lace cover, three lace options
Out 27 Nov, AUD 280

stories.h: Noah x Converse Chuck 70 in woven Black Watch tartan
stories.why: Grunge-plaid Chucks, easy tomboy staple
sum: Noah and Converse released a Chuck 70 Ox on 19 November. The navy-and-green Black Watch tartan is woven into a three-tone canvas, not printed, which gives the check more texture.

Noah modelled the build on 1990s Chucks: the wing tongue stitch is gone, a woven tongue tag replaces it, and the shoe sits on a light-brown gum sole for a vintage look. It has an OrthoLite insole and very little branding. It follows the pair's plaid Chuck 70 capsule from spring 2026 and is sold through Converse and Noah.
pts: Woven tartan canvas, not a print
1990s details and gum sole
Out 19 Nov at Converse and Noah

stories.h: Jae Tips' Nike Air Bakin Low gets a chile red pair
stories.why: Loud, colorful basketball low
sum: Bronx designer Jae Tips, who once worked at Foot Locker, has shown a second colorway of his first Nike collab, the late-'90s Air Bakin Low. This one is white and chile red with green camo underlays and a bright green lining.

Small details nod to his label Savior Worldwide: toe Swooshes shaped like an S, Savior branding on the heel, and oversized multicolor Air lettering. It follows a black-and-purple pair teased before ComplexCon. Both are due in spring 2027 for $160.
pts: White and chile red with green camo
S-shaped Swooshes for Savior Worldwide
Spring 2027, $160

stories.h: Indie shoe brands to try, including Bali's DIRT
stories.why: Niche labels, an Indonesian brand
sum: Hypebae's winter roundup of independent footwear labels for anyone tired of sneakers: AnnK, a Paris label making convertible riding boots in Kyiv; Swedish minimalist Vagabond; Miista from East London, known for odd shapes and textures; Lili Curia, a newcomer from 2025 working between London and Florence; and Le Monde Beryl's Italian-made slippers and flats.
Closest to home is DIRT, founded in Bali in 2020 by Andrea Norberg and Sarah Doyle. It mixes '90s nostalgia with square toes, bubble soles and slouchy washed leather, and has recently added swimwear.
pts: Six indie labels, from playful to minimal
DIRT is Bali-founded, '90s-inspired and chunky
Miista and AnnK for experimental shapes

stories.h: Willy Chavarria launches his first handbags
stories.why: Bags with attitude, not logo basics
sum: Willy Chavarria has released his first full handbag line, made by hand in Italy. The Bronca, inspired by 1960s bags, has a leather-covered metal frame, a rounded tube handle and W-shaped straps. The W Slouch is a soft, roomy shape with a removable padded handle and an adjustable shoulder strap.

Both have W details, antiqued brass or matte silver hardware, and branded carabiners holding a set of Willy Chavarria keys. Chavarria says he made them because everyone seems to carry the same few bags. Pre-orders are open on his site, and they ship 4 December.
pts: Two styles: the structured Bronca and the soft W Slouch
Made in Italy, carabiner and key details
Pre-order now, out 4 Dec

stories.h: Shanghai's underground club kids and Nu China style
stories.why: Asian street style, playful and niche
sum: Dazed photographed ravers at a Live From Earth x Eastern Margins night in Shanghai, headlined by rapper Billionhappy. They show Nu China style: young Chinese people reworking subcultures they find online through a local lens. It's eclectic and hard to label.

People talked about orange Martine Rose camo pants, an anime tracksuit from Chinese indie label SelfishGhost, rainbow bear shoes, and worn-in jackets from Shanghai's Lingshi Road vintage market. Most described clubs as judgement-free places where campy, playful outfits help people connect.
pts: Nu China: online subcultures, worn the local way
Indie Chinese labels and vintage-market finds
Bright, playful outfits made for dancing

stories.h: Hong Kong street style: thrift, DIY and local labels
stories.why: Casual, individual Asian street style
sum: Photographer Jaison Lin came home to Hong Kong after five years away to shoot what young creatives wear, eat and listen to there in 2026. Many outfits are thrifted or home-made: HK$50 Salvation Army trousers, jeans students sewed themselves, and jewelry from friends' small brands like ROKUNEN.

Others mix in Rick Owens, Guidi, Camper boots and a Vietnamese label, Dayla Studio. The subjects also share local tips, from the Salvation Army in Chai Wan to a giant costume store in Kwun Tong and the Sai Kung rock pools.
pts: Thrift and DIY over head-to-toe brands
Small Asian labels from friends
Local tips: thrift stores, costume shops, raves

stories.h: Gucci to show in Shanghai, sacai in Hong Kong
stories.why: Big fashion moves heading to Asia
sum: Hypebeast's weekly roundup leans toward Asia. Gucci will hold its Cruise 2028 show in Shanghai on 17 May 2027, Demna's first show there, marking 30 years since the house's first store in the region. sacai will hold its first Hong Kong runway show at the HSBC Main Building on 13 December.

Elsewhere, Gentle Monster released a Jonathan Glazer film starring Joaquin Phoenix for its smart glasses, which launch in the US and Korea on 10 December. BEAMS also marked its 50th anniversary with a 14-piece adidas pack built around two loafers.
pts: Gucci Cruise 2028 in Shanghai, May 2027
sacai's first Hong Kong show, 13 Dec
Gentle Monster smart glasses; BEAMS x adidas loafers

stories.h: World Court finds Myanmar guilty of Rohingya genocide
stories.why: Justice for a persecuted Muslim people
sum: On 19 November the International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the mostly Muslim Rohingya during the military's 2017 campaign in Rakhine State. The case was brought by The Gambia in 2019. It is the first time the court has held a state responsible for genocide; in 2007 it stopped short of that over Srebrenica.

Amnesty's Agnes Callamard called it a rare moment of justice for survivors. Amnesty notes the court said genocidal intent can coexist with military aims, which matters for South Africa's case against Israel. It wants a UN arms embargo, an ICC referral and reparations for the roughly 1.3 million Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh.
pts: First ICJ ruling holding a state responsible for genocide
Myanmar ordered to pay reparations and allow safe return
Amnesty: reasoning on intent bears on the Gaza case

stories.h: What the Rohingya ruling could mean for Gaza
stories.why: Legal path to accountability for Gaza
sum: Al Jazeera looks at how the ICJ's Myanmar verdict could shape South Africa's genocide case against Israel. Nine of the 15 judges found genocide was the only reasonable inference from the evidence. That sets a precedent for proving a state's intent without written orders, and it rejects self-defence as a cover. Analysts quoted say it will not decide the Gaza case but may shape how it is judged.

South Africa filed in December 2023. Its next submission is due in November 2027, and a final judgment is years away. The article cites about 75,000 killed in Gaza, roughly 1,660 of them since the October 2025 ceasefire. It also notes US pressure on international courts and Nicaragua's pending case against Germany over arms sales.
pts: Ruling makes intent easier to prove without explicit orders
Gaza case judgment still years away
Countries that arm Israel could face accessory claims

stories.h: Israeli drones kill seven in central Gaza despite truce
stories.why: The ceasefire is not stopping the killing
sum: Medical sources told Al Jazeera that Israeli attacks killed at least seven Palestinians in central Gaza on Friday. Four died when a drone struck a group in Bureij refugee camp, and two near the entrance to Deir el-Balah. Another body was taken to al-Awda Hospital from Nuseirat. The wounded went to hospitals that are short of supplies and staff, and the army carried out more demolitions in Shujaiya and east of Khan Younis.

Al Jazeera says more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire. On World Children's Day, Palestinian prisoner groups said about 350 Palestinian children are held in Israeli prisons.
pts: Seven killed in drone strikes, per medical sources
Over 1,600 reported killed since the ceasefire
Prisoner groups say about 350 children are detained

stories.h: Israeli-backed Gaza militias linked to Nuseirat raid
stories.why: How the occupation works through proxies
sum: An anonymous Palestinian security source told Al Jazeera that Israel-funded anti-Hamas groups took part in this week's Israeli ground operation near Nuseirat and Bureij camps, terrorising civilians under Israeli fire cover. The operation was the first announced push west of the Yellow Line since the ceasefire. Gaza's Government Media Office says about 6,000 people fled. Israel says it targeted a tunnel.

Analysts quoted say about five militia factions with several hundred members have spread from Rafah into central Gaza. They compare the arrangement to Israel's former South Lebanon Army proxy. Israel has openly acknowledged backing such groups. The main claims rely on anonymous sources and were not independently verified.
pts: Militias accused of joining the first post-truce ground push
About 6,000 displaced, per Gaza's media office
Analysts warn of a lasting Israeli proxy force

stories.h: Walhi: half of this year's fire hotspots on company land
stories.why: Corporate land grabs and impunity for burning
sum: Mongabay reports that Prabowo's haze apology at the ASEAN summit means little without action against corporations. Walhi says half of the 30,927 hotspots recorded from January to September were inside palm oil and timber concessions. It names groups such as Sinar Mas and Wilmar, and offshore owners in Singapore, Malaysia and secrecy jurisdictions.

Walhi also counts 807 hotspots in Merauke's state-backed food and energy estates. It argues the government agencies running those projects share the blame. Walhi and the Kuala Institute say the state goes after small farmers and indigenous burning customs rather than big firms. They call for permits to be reviewed and revoked and financing to be cut off. Some named companies deny links.
pts: About 50% of hotspots fell in concessions, per Walhi
807 hotspots in Merauke national strategic projects
Critics say indigenous communities blamed instead of firms

stories.h: Gibran's exit hands Prabowo near-total control
stories.why: Democratic backsliding and shrinking civic space
sum: In this analysis, Medan lecturer Puteri Atikah reviews Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's 12 November resignation. It followed a Supreme Court ruling that annulled the school certificate he used to qualify in 2024. The day before, 120 lawmakers from all eight factions had backed a motion that could have led to impeachment.

She argues that Gibran's exit removes the last check on Prabowo and weakens Jokowi's network, with seven of eight parties already in the ruling coalition. She points to centralised flagship programmes, a growing military role in civilian life, critics labelled foreign lackeys, and arrests of protesters. Together, she says, these mark the end of the Reformasi era.
pts: Resignation came a day before a possible impeachment step
Seven of eight DPR parties back Prabowo
Author warns of tighter control over dissent

stories.h: Mondoweiss founder at 20 years: AIPAC is finished
stories.why: The antizionist movement's growing reach
sum: Marking Mondoweiss's 20th anniversary, founder Phil Weiss tells the site's US correspondent Michael Arria how talking about the Israel lobby went from taboo to mainstream. He argues that AIPAC, despite decades of success at keeping US and Israeli policy aligned, is now politically toxic and finished as a force. He also says J Street is running out of room because it avoids Gaza.

Weiss notes Democratic leaders distancing themselves from Netanyahu. He points to Abdul El-Sayed's Senate win and proposals to end US military aid as signs of change. He warns that these shifts are still defensive and that continued US support keeps Palestinians suffering, but says he is optimistic.
pts: Weiss says AIPAC is now toxic to many Democrats
Debate over US aid to Israel moving into Congress
Anniversary of a key antizionist outlet
